defects.claim: Inverse mapping divides by the raw range difference, which overflows on a wide finite range: the midpoint inverts to domain[0] and the far endpoint to NaN
defects.scenario: Output range spanning opposite-sign finite extremes (e.g. [-MAX_VALUE, MAX_VALUE]): the range difference overflows to Infinity, so inverting the midpoint returns domain[0] and inverting the far endpoint gives NaN

defects.claim: onGrid sets decimal places from the step's magnitude, so a step of 0.25 rounds 0.75 to 0.8 and stepTicks returns ticks off the grid or out of bounds
defects.scenario: stepTicks with step 0.25: a tick at 0.75 comes back as 0.8
defects.cause: precision taken from magnitude, not step digits

defects.claim: The log scale constructor builds the full unthinned powerTicks array only to test whether it has two entries, which blows up for a base near 1
defects.scenario: A valid base close to 1 makes the exponent interval huge; the up-front scan dominates scale creation even when few ticks are eventually wanted
